title: ESP32-C6-DevKitM-1
notes: Not broken out: GPIO10/11 (the ESP32-C6FH4 in the ESP32-C6-MINI-1 has an in-package flash and does not lead them out) and GPIO24-30 (in-package flash); all other GPIOs are on J1/J3.
Strapping pins on the headers: GPIO4 (MTMS), GPIO5 (MTDI), GPIO8 (RGB LED), GPIO9 and GPIO15.
TX/RX (GPIO16/GPIO17) are U0TXD/U0RXD on the USB-to-UART bridge.
GPIO12/GPIO13 are USB_D-/USB_D+ of the USB-Serial/JTAG port (J3-14/J3-13); used as normal GPIOs, USB-JTAG stops working.
Standard module: ESP32-C6-MINI-1 (ESP32-C6-DevKitM-1-N4: 4 MB flash, no PSRAM; module variant mini-1). The guide also names ESP32-C6-MINI-1U with an external antenna connector.
Power the board one way only: the USB ports, or the 5V and GND pins, or the 3V3 and GND pins (the guide calls them mutually exclusive).
The guide labels J1-7 and J1-8 '0/N' and '1/N' (GPIO0/GPIO1 with XTAL_32K_P/XTAL_32K_N); it does not explain the '/N' suffix.
J1 is drawn on the left and J3 on the right (USB at the bottom) as on the other Espressif DevKits; the guide's pin layout figure is not in the pinned corpus, so the side is unverified.

row: The USB Type-C port on the ESP32-C6 chip compliant with USB 2.0 full speed. It is capable of up to 12 Mbps transfer speed (Note that this port does not support the faster 480 Mbps high-speed transfer mode). This port is used for power supply to the board, for flashing applications to the chip, for communication with the chip using USB protocols, as well as for JTAG debugging.

citations.quote: GPIO12 and GPIO13 are used by USB-JTAG by default. If they are reconfigured to operate as normal GPIOs, USB-JTAG functionality will be disabled.

row: Single USB-to-UART bridge chip provides transfer rates up to 3 Mbps.
Used for power supply to the board, for flashing applications to the chip, as well as the communication with the ESP32-C6 chip via the on-board USB-to-UART bridge.
All available GPIO pins (except for the SPI bus for flash) are broken out to the pin headers on the board.

citations.quote: GPIO24 ~ GPIO30 are usually used for SPI flash and not recommended for other uses.

For chip variants with an SiP flash built in, GPIO24 ~ GPIO30 are dedicated to connecting the SiP flash; GPIO10 ~ GPIO11 are not led out to any chip pins; therefore, only the remaining 22 GPIO pins are available.
The module is built around the ESP32-C6FH4 chip, which has a 4 MB flash in the chip's package.
.. [3] MTMS, MTDI, GPIO8, GPIO9, and GPIO15 are strapping pins of the ESP32-C6 chip.
GPIO4, GPIO5, GPIO8, GPIO9, and GPIO15 are strapping pins.
